design_detail: Structural MRI and inhibitory-control testing in stimulant-dependent individuals, their non-dependent biological siblings, and unrelated healthy controls.
can_establish: Which brain-structure and behavioural differences are shared by siblings who do not use stimulants, and therefore cannot be effects of the drug.
cannot_establish: Which differences in people who use stimulants are drug-induced (shared differences could still be worsened by use); generalization beyond the recruited families.

sample.selection_effects: Families willing to participate; dependent individuals with an unaffected sibling may differ from those without.

exposure.measurement: Clinical diagnosis of stimulant dependence (cocaine or amphetamine) [to be extracted from PDF]

comparison.controls: Unrelated healthy volunteers and unaffected siblings.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: The sibling design is the best available proxy for premorbid status.

outcomes.instruments: Structural MRI (fronto-striatal regions, white matter); stop-signal reaction time.
outcomes.operationalization: Group differences shared by probands and siblings vs. unique to probands.

interpretation_gap.results_show: Siblings shared fronto-striatal abnormalities and poorer inhibitory control with probands, indicating a familial, pre-existing component.
interpretation_gap.claimed: Reported as evidence of 'vulnerability'; some coverage overstated this as showing that drug-related brain differences are all pre-existing, which the design does not show.

replication.where_it_stands: Sibling and twin designs consistently find pre-existing components; magnitude varies.

funding.funder: [to be extracted from PDF] (Medical Research Council, UK, likely)

what_would_settle_it: Longitudinal sibling cohorts followed from before onset of use.

domains.note: Sibling design controls much, not all.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: Strong design for the question it asks.
